arxiv-2109-06662.title: Identifying Partial Mouse Brain Microscopy Images from the Allen Reference Atlas using a Contrastively Learned Semantic Space
arxiv-2109-06662.creator: Justinas Antanavicius, Roberto Leiras, Raghavendra Selvan
arxiv-2109-06662.description: Abstract Registering mouse brain microscopy images to a reference atlas is crucial to determine the locations of anatomical structures in the brain, which is an essential step for understanding the function of brain circuits. Most existing registration pipelines assume the identity of the reference plate – to which the image slice is to be registered – is known beforehand.

arxiv-2201-03705.title: Quantum Measurement Without Collapse
arxiv-2201-03705.creator: Pavel Bóna
arxiv-2201-03705.description: Abstract It is shown that the classical book by von Neumann proposing dynamics of measured systems with “reduction (or collapse) of system’s wave packet” contains also hints how to avoid this discontinuity in time evolution of the measured system (hence it is in this point not quite selfconsistent).

arxiv-2211-02503.title: On convergence and singularity of conditional copulas of multivariate Archimedean copulas, and estimating conditional dependence
arxiv-2211-02503.creator: Thimo M. Kasper
arxiv-2211-02503.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Thimo M. Kasper. The present contribution derives an explicit expression for (a version of) every uni- and multivariate conditional distribution (i.e., Markov kernel) of Archimedean copulas and uses this representation to generalize a recently established result, saying that in the class of multivariate Archimedean copulas standard uniform convergence implies weak convergence of almost all univariate Markov kernels, to arbitrary multivariate Markov kernels. Moreover, we prove that an Archimedean copula is singular if, and only if, almost all uni- and multivariate Markov kernels are singular.

arxiv-2211-17237.title: Behavior of Gordian graphs at infinity Thanks: The work is supported by Ministry of Science and Higher Education of the Russian Federation, agreement № 075–15–2019–1620
arxiv-2211-17237.creator: Alexey Yu. Miller
arxiv-2211-17237.description: Abstract . The present paper refers to the knot theory and is devoted to the study of global properties of Gordian graphs of various local moves. In 2005, Gambaudo and Ghys raised the question of the behavior at infinity of the crossing change Gordian graph. They proposed studying its “ends”, that is, unbounded connected components of complements of bounded subsets.

arxiv-2212-11265.title: Detecting and characterizing pulsar haloes with the Cherenkov Telescope Array 2022 Detecting and characterizing pulsar haloes with the Cherenkov Telescope Array –
arxiv-2212-11265.creator: Christopher Eckner, Veronika Vodeb, Pierrick Martin, Gabrijela Zaharijas, Francesca Calore
arxiv-2212-11265.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Christopher Eckner, Veronika Vodeb, Pierrick Martin, Gabrijela Zaharijas, Francesca Calore. The recently identified source class of pulsar haloes may be numerous and bright enough in the TeV range to constitute a large fraction of the sources that will be observed with the Cherenkov Telescope Array (CTA).

arxiv-2312-14025.title: L p L^{p} -cohomology for higher rank spaces and groups: critical exponents and rigidity
arxiv-2312-14025.creator: Marc Bourdon and Bertrand Rémy
arxiv-2312-14025.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Marc Bourdon and Bertrand Rémy. We initiate the investigation of critical exponents (in degree equal to the rank) for the vanishing of L p L^{p} -cohomology of higher rank Lie groups and related manifolds. We deal with the rank 2 case and exhibit such phenomena for SL 3 ​ ( 𝐑 ) {\rm SL}_{3}({\bf R}) and for a family of 5-dimensional solvable Lie groups. We use the critical exponents to compare the groups up to quasi-isometry.

arxiv-2401-06986.title: Learning driving style embedding from GPS-derived moving patterns for driver identification
arxiv-2401-06986.creator: Lin Lu
arxiv-2401-06986.description: Abstract Learning fingerprint-like driving style representations is crucial to accurately identify who is behind the wheel in open driving situations. This study explores the learning of driving styles with GPS signals that are currently available in connected vehicles for short-term driver identification. First, an input driving trajectory is windowed into subtrajectories with fixed time lengths.

arxiv-2401-15656.title: Dynamically Allocated Interval-Based Generative Linguistic Steganography with Roulette Wheel
arxiv-2401-15656.creator: Yihao Wang, Ruiqi Song, Lingxiao Li, Ru Zhang *, Jianyi Liu
arxiv-2401-15656.description: Abstract Existing linguistic steganography schemes often overlook the conditional probability (CP) of tokens in the candidate pool, allocating the one coding to all tokens, which results in identical selection likelihoods. This approach leads to the selection of low-CP tokens, degrading the quality of stegos and making them more detectable.

arxiv-2402-07865.title: Prismatic VLMs: Investigating the Design Space of Visually-Conditioned Language Models
arxiv-2402-07865.creator: Siddharth Karamcheti, Suraj Nair, Ashwin Balakrishna, Percy Liang, Thomas Kollar, Dorsa Sadigh
arxiv-2402-07865.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Siddharth Karamcheti, Suraj Nair, Ashwin Balakrishna, Percy Liang, Thomas Kollar, Dorsa Sadigh. Visually-conditioned language models (VLMs) have seen growing adoption in applications such as visual dialogue, scene understanding, and robotic task planning; adoption that has fueled a wealth of new models such as LLaVa, InstructBLIP, and PaLI-3.

arxiv-2403-08704.title: Limits on the OH Molecule in the Smith High Velocity Cloud Facilities: GBT, IRSA
arxiv-2403-08704.creator: Anthony H. Minter, Felix J. Lockman, S. A. Balashev, H. Alyson Ford
arxiv-2403-08704.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Anthony H. Minter, Felix J. Lockman, S. A. Balashev, H. Alyson Ford. We have used the Green Bank Telescope (GBT) to search for the O H molecule at several locations in the Smith Cloud, one of the most prominent of the high-velocity clouds that surround the Milky Way.

arxiv-2411-07533.title: Large Language Models as Neurolinguistic Subjects: Discrepancy between Performance and Competence
arxiv-2411-07533.creator: Linyang He, Ercong Nie, Helmut Schmid, Hinrich Schütze Nima Mesgarani Jonathan Brennan
arxiv-2411-07533.description: Abstract This study investigates the linguistic understanding of Large Language Models (LLMs) regarding signifier (form) and signified (meaning) by distinguishing two LLM assessment paradigms: psycholinguistic and neurolinguistic. Traditional psycholinguistic evaluations often reflect statistical rules that may not accurately represent LLMs’ true linguistic competence.

arxiv-2502-01703.title: QLESS: A Quantized Approach for Data Valuation and Selection in Large Language Model Fine-Tuning
arxiv-2502-01703.creator: Moses Ananta, Muhammad Farid Adilazuarda, Zayd Muhammad Kawakibi Zuhri, Ayu Purwarianti, Alham Fikri Aji
arxiv-2502-01703.description: Abstract Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) is often constrained by the computational costs of processing massive datasets. We propose QLESS (Quantized Low-rank Gradient Similarity Search), which integrates gradient quantization with the LESS framework to enable memory-efficient data valuation and selection.

arxiv-2506-11614.title: Accelerating Delta Debugging through Probabilistic Monotonicity Assessment Conference: The 29th International Conference on Evaluation and Assessment in Software Engineering; 17–20 June, 2025; Istanbul, Türkiye DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06 CCS: Software and its engineering Soft
arxiv-2506-11614.creator: Yonggang Tao, Jingling Xue
arxiv-2506-11614.description: Abstract . Delta debugging assumes search space monotonicity: if a program causes a failure, any supersets of that program will also induce the same failure, permitting the exclusion of subsets of non-failure-inducing programs. However, this assumption does not always hold in practice.

arxiv-2510-21418.title: DreamerV3-XP: Optimizing exploration through uncertainty estimation
arxiv-2510-21418.creator: Lukas Bierling, Davide Pasero, Jan Henrik Bertrand, Kiki van Gerwen
arxiv-2510-21418.description: Abstract We introduce DreamerV3-XP , an extension of DreamerV3 that improves exploration and learning efficiency. This includes (i) a prioritized replay buffer, scoring trajectories by return, reconstruction loss, and value error and (ii) an intrinsic reward based on disagreement over predicted environment rewards from an ensemble of world models.

arxiv-2512-10939.title: GaussianHeadTalk: Wobble-Free 3D Talking Heads with Audio Driven Gaussian Splatting
arxiv-2512-10939.creator: Madhav Agarwal, Mingtian Zhang, Laura Sevilla-Lara, Steven McDonagh
arxiv-2512-10939.description: Abstract Speech-driven talking heads have recently emerged and enable interactive avatars. However, real-world applications are limited, as current methods achieve high visual fidelity but slow or fast yet temporally unstable. Diffusion methods provide realistic image generation, yet struggle with one-shot settings.

pmc-10655314.title: Toxic posterior segment syndrome with retinal vasculitis likely caused by intraocular cotton fiber after vitreoretinal surgery – a case report
pmc-10655314.creator: Chaitra Jayadev, Aditi Gupta, Santosh Gopikrishna Gadde, Ramesh Venkatesh
pmc-10655314.description: BackgroundIntraocular inflammation is common after anterior or posterior segment surgery. They typically manifest either as non-infectious inflammation of the anterior or posterior segment, known as toxic anterior or posterior segment syndrome (TPSS), or as sterile or infective endophthalmitis. In this report, we describe a rare case of TPSS following vitreoretinal surgery, presenting as hemorrhagic retinal vasculitis.

pmc-11570485.title: Progressive transcriptomic shifts in evolved yeast strains following gene knockout
pmc-11570485.creator: Bei Jiang, Chuyao Xiao, Li Liu
pmc-11570485.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SummaryGene knockout disrupts cellular homeostasis, altering gene expression, and phenotypes. We investigated whether cells return to their pre-knockout transcriptomic state through adaptive evolution experiments on hap4Δ and ade1Δ yeast strains. Analysis revealed that genes with higher expression levels and more physical interaction partners in wild-type strains were more likely to be restored, suggesting that genes of significant functional importance have increased resilience to genetic perturbations. However, as the experiment progressed, most initially restored genes became unrestored.

pmc-11691801.description: This study explores the determinants influencing collaboration between Community Comprehensive Support Centers (CCSCs) and Domestic Violence (DV) support agencies in addressing cases of older Intimate Partner Violence (IPV) in Japan. pmc-12537810.title: Uterine Intravenous Leiomyomatosis with Internal Iliac Artery Involvement
pmc-12537810.creator: Meizheng Dang, Shangwen Cai, Jin Yao, Buyi Zhang, Lili Zhang, Wen Xu, Pintong Huang
pmc-12537810.description: BackgroundIntravenous leiomyomatosis (IVL) is a rare benign uterine smooth muscle tumor that typically spreads along venous channels. Arterial extension is exceedingly uncommon but presents greater surgical challenges and may adversely affect prognosis.Case ReportWe describe a case of IVL extending into the internal iliac artery in a 32-year-old woman.

pmc-12635673.title: Unraveling the role of dysfunctional sleep beliefs: How chronotype shapes sleep quality and academic success in medical students
pmc-12635673.creator: Şengül Tosun Altınöz, Leman Deniz Tarlacık, Esin Engin, Yaren Uzel, Uğur Doğan, Ali Ercan Altınöz
pmc-12635673.description: BACKGROUNDDysfunctional beliefs about sleep may influence academic performance through their impact on sleep quality. Differences in chronotype can further moderate this relationship, particularly among students with irregular sleep patterns.AIMTo examine the indirect effects of dysfunctional beliefs about sleep on academic performance through sleep quality while considering individual differences in chronotypes among medical students.

pmc-12735869.title: MicroRNAs in Breast Cancer Bone Metastasis Formation and Progression: An Overview on Recent Progress in This Research Field
pmc-12735869.creator: Margherita Puppo
pmc-12735869.description: Bone metastasis is a common and severe complication in advanced stages of breast cancer (BC) that is characterised by limited treatment options and poor patient prognosis. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are a large class of regulatory small non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) expressed by cells. Moreover, miRNAs can be released by cells into the blood and lymphatic streams, acting as distant cell-to-cell communicators.

pmc-12789093.title: Molecular architecture of the human TRPC1/C5 heteromeric channel
pmc-12789093.creator: Sun-Hong Kim, Hyunwoo Park, Jinhyeong Kim, Hana Kang, Jongdae Won, Byoung-Cheol Lee, Insuk So, Hyung Ho Lee
pmc-12789093.description: Transient receptor potential (TRP) ion channels form heteromers through combinatorial associations of distinct subunits, contributing to the diversity of TRP channel functions. Among them, TRPC5, which forms a heteromer with TRPC1, represents an attractive pharmaceutical target for treating anxiety and depression.

pmc-12960591.title: Glucose metabolic dysregulation of diabetes and Its role in atrial fibrillation pathogenesis
pmc-12960591.creator: Yuqi Chen, Min Xu, Ke Wei, Nan Ma
pmc-12960591.description: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most prevalent persistent arrhythmia in clinical practice, with a complex pathogenesis that remains incompletely understood. Emerging evidence underscores a strong association between diabetes and the occurrence of AF, highlighting a significantly elevated risk among diabetic patients.

pmc-13163810.title: Signaling Pathway Dissection After Progesterone Receptor Enhancement in an Immortalized Pre-Cancer Fallopian Tube Epithelial Cell Line
pmc-13163810.creator: Yu-Hsun Chang, Kun-Chi Wu, Dah-Ching Ding
pmc-13163810.description: Ovarian cancer remains the most lethal gynecologic malignancy, with the majority of patients presenting at advanced stages and exhibiting poor long-term survival. High-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC), the predominant subtype, likely originates from fallopian tube epithelial cells (FTECs), whose biology is strongly influenced by hormonal signaling.

pmc-13326200.title: Platypnea-Orthodeoxia Syndrome in a Patient With Aortic Root Dilation and a Patent Foramen Ovale
pmc-13326200.creator: AK Prohl, S Kwiatkowski, A Samanta, SN Hong-Zohlman, H Allaham, L Forbess
pmc-13326200.description: BackgroundPlatypnea-orthodeoxia syndrome (POS) is a rare condition characterized by dyspnea and hypoxemia in the upright position that improves when supine.Case SummaryA 75-year-old man presented with dyspnea and chronic hypoxemic respiratory failure of unknown etiology. The patient was dyspneic sitting and standing and was free of symptoms when supine.

pmc-13437706.title: Maternal psychopathic traits prospectively predict youth callous-unemotional traits
pmc-13437706.creator: Nicholas D. Thomson, Jessica J. James
pmc-13437706.description: BackgroundCallous-unemotional (CU) traits identify a subgroup of youth with conduct disorder (CD) at heightened risk for persistent antisocial behavior and poor long-term outcomes. Although parental psychopathic traits have been associated with offspring CU traits, less is known about whether specific psychopathic facets uniquely predict adolescent CU trajectories beyond baseline CU traits, particularly among youth diagnosed with CD.

pmc-13601604.creator: Julia R Yamazaki-Tan, Alexandra I Manta, Mark H B Radford
